Prepare, wait for the organization's turn, then admit under the row lock.

`X-Celesto-Client` (ui, sdk or mcp) records which surface made the
sandbox; without it the credential type decides (see resolve_rest_origin).

The wait for the turn holds no pooled connection, so a burst from one
organization cannot empty the pool for everyone else. The sandbox-created
alert goes to the broker after the response is sent, so neither the
organization's turn nor the client waits on it.

Queue the command, then wait for its result on the event loop.

The wait is woken by the host's result (Redis `pool:op:<id>`) or by the
fallback tick; each check ends its read transaction, so a slow command
holds no pooled connection. A cancelled wait still expires the command
(D-25, see `ComputePoolService.exec`).

schema.title: Response Open Session V1 Internal Pool Hosts  Host Id  Session Post

post.description:
Deliver the next command, holding an empty poll open for a wake-up when the host supports it.

Hosts that advertised `long_poll` wait here for up to POOL_LONG_POLL_SECONDS
(+/- jitter), then poll once more. The hold ends early on a `pool:host:<id>`
publish or when its fallback check finds a pending command, which it runs
every POOL_WAKEUP_TICK_SECONDS. The hold runs on the event loop and holds
no database connection between checks. Older hosts get today's immediate
answer.

CustomTemplateLogsResponse.title: CustomTemplateLogsResponse
CustomTemplateLogsResponse.description:
The end of the latest build's log.

``log`` is empty until the build worker has copied the first bytes.
It holds at most the last 256 KB: ``offset`` is the byte position in the
whole log where ``log`` starts, and ``truncated`` is True when earlier
bytes were left out. ``size`` is how many log bytes are stored; send it
back as ``known_size`` and, while it has not changed, the answer is
``unchanged: true`` with an empty ``log`` (keep showing the last one).
